newsitem.title: FRANCE: Lagardere interested in Thomson-CSF - paper. [CORRECTED 10:50 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Lagardere interested in Thomson-CSF - paper. [CORRECTED 10:50 GMT]

text.p: (Corrects headline to make clear La Tribune newspaper, not Thomson-CSF, is the source of the story).

French conglomerate Lagardere would consider taking part in the privatisation of defence electronics firm Thomson-CSF as long as only a small part of the company were sold through a public share offering, La Tribune newspaper said on Friday.
It said Lagardere chairman Noel Forgeard was not opposed to the possibility of a privatisation combining placements in Thomson-CSF and a share offering "on condition that the latter remain marginal."
Lagardere officials were not immediately available for comment.

Another newspaper, Les Echos, also said on Friday that Forgeard had backed down from his previous stance opposing any public share offering in Thomson-CSF but that Forgeard still wanted the bulk sold through private placements.
The government is expected to announce the terms of the privatisation of Thomson-CSF, 58 percent owned by state company Thomson SA, later this month or in early February.
In December it scrapped a previous plan to sell Thomson in one block to Lagardere after France's independent privatisation commission objected to the terms.
The French government now plans to sell Thomson-CSF and Thomson's other business, loss-making television manufacturer Thomson Multimedia, separately.
Thomson-CSF's management is reported to favour a privatisation through a public share offering.
Lagardere, which proposes to merge its Matra missiles unit with Thomson-CSF to create a big French defence company, had feared a public offering of Thomson-CSF would risk breaking up the company.

La Tribune also said Lagardere was seeking to finalise a missiles agreement with a German partner this year to avoid the appearance it was too closely tied to British interests because of its partnerships in space activities with General Electric Plc and in missiles with British Aerospace.
